remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch in required materials.
No admissible evidence shows an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this exact limitation.

The policy text makes weaknesses material when they affect a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, and the record still indicates the enterprise refund workflow is tied to a renewal success plan.
Legal review on disclosure remains open, and the policy text says low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, and public governance guidance support operational readiness but do not satisfy the stated internal disclosure predicate.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence. The response is a narrower interpretation of the same record, not new proof. That narrower posture is more careful, but it still leaves the core compliance predicate unresolved: under the stated policy, a material limitation affecting a named launch use case or contractual customer segment must be disclosed before launch unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. The current record still lacks evidence of disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or a contrary legal/policy determination. That means the issue is not merely a caveat attached to an otherwise satisfied requirement; it is an unresolved condition for compliance itself. A caveated business case for launch may be operationally understandable, but on the admissible record it is not enough to move this to compliant_with_caveats.
